comments.note: Edge case noted: configActiveTab is a module-level singleton that persists across fresh data reloads (e.g., navigating away and back to Config). This is intentional SPA UX — the user's last active tab is remembered. configDirty is always reset on fresh load (renderConfigPage line 40), so there is no stale dirty state risk. No action required.

Edge case verified: the unsaved-changes guard correctly handles all three tabs. For General tab discard, no extra module-level state reset is needed (General tab has no module-level state — config is read from DOM on submit). For modelRegistry and personaModels, the guard resets their respective module-level state variables. Logic is correct and complete.
No issues observed — config.js is clean, responsibility-scoped, and all cross-tab dirty-tracking via the shared global configDirty object works correctly with the extracted tab files.

summary: [PASS] config.js reviewed in full (181 lines). The coordinator is well-structured, responsibility-scoped, and clean after the extraction work. No blocking issues found. Two Fix-Forward items applied (comment improvements). One documentation-forward tag raised for the configDirty global contract. Cross-module dirty-tracking architecture is sound; tab-switching guard logic is correct and covers all three tabs including the General tab's stateless design.

comments.note: config.js is correctly scoped to three responsibilities: (1) module-level state (configActiveTab, configDirty), (2) the page scaffold and tab-bar event handler, (3) the General tab render + event wiring. This is a clean, durable shape — if either companion module grows, no surgery to this coordinator is needed.

The Promise.all pattern in renderConfig() is correctly defensive: it guards each optional API call with a fallback (API.getModels ? ... : Promise.resolve([])). This ensures the General-tab-only path still works even if companion API endpoints are not yet registered, which is appropriate for a progressively-expanded SPA.

The unsaved-changes guard at lines 65–75 correctly resets module-level state for modelRegistry and personaModels tabs on discard. The General tab requires no state reset (it is stateless at module level — config is read from the DOM on submit). This asymmetry is intentional and correct.

The chained assignment at line 40 (configDirty.general = configDirty.personaModels = configDirty.modelRegistry = false) and lines 41–43 (mrModels = mrOriginal = mrEditingId = null, etc.) are idiomatic JS but mix two styles: the configDirty chain uses property access on a single object (fine), while the mr*/pm* chains reset multiple independent variables in a single expression. Both are correct and readable. The Developer's implementation note already flagged the style divergence — no action required, but it is worth preserving the awareness for future contributors.

Applied Fix-Forward: improved the file-header 'Depends on' comment to explicitly name `configDirty` as a module-level global that config.js owns and the companion tab files read. Before: 'Depends on: API, UI, escapeHtml, showLoading, showError'. After: 'Depends on: API, UI, escapeHtml, showLoading, showError | Exports (global): configDirty (shared with config-model-registry.js, config-persona-models.js)'. This makes the cross-file ownership contract visible at the top of the file, reducing future contributor confusion about where configDirty originates. No behavioral change.

Applied Fix-Forward: added an inline clarifying comment on the configDirty declaration block (lines 12–17) noting that the object is mutated directly by companion modules (config-model-registry.js writes .modelRegistry, config-persona-models.js writes .personaModels). Preserves object identity — companion files hold a reference to this object, not a copy. This surfaces the shared-mutable-global pattern documented in KN-0045 so future readers understand why reassignment (= {}) is not used here.

[documentation-forward] The configDirty global contract (declared in config.js, mutated by all three tab modules, object identity must be preserved) is currently documented only via inline comments scattered across three files. The Documentation agent should add a brief architecture note — either in the file header of config.js or a companion ARCHITECTURE.md — describing the shared-mutable-object pattern, load order requirement, and the rule that companion files must never reassign configDirty (only mutate its properties). This is the primary implicit contract that would be invisible to a new contributor joining the codebase.
